newsitem.title: USA: TECNOL sees Q3 charge of $0.02 a share.
newsitem.headline: TECNOL sees Q3 charge of $0.02 a share.

text.p: TECNOL Medical Products Inc on Monday said it will take a one-time, pre-tax charge of about $600,000, or $0.02 per share on a tax-affected basis, in the third quarter ended August 31.

The charge is due to a settlement of a class action lawsuit brought against the company and some of its senior executives a year ago in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas, TECNOL said.
The tentative agreement provides for a settlement payment of $2.2 million, most of which will be covered by TECNOL's directors' and officers' insurance carrier.

TECNOL said its management was convinced it would have ultimately prevailed in the lawsuit, but moved to settle the suit before substantial legal fees and management time were spent. The suit was related to timing with which the company disclosed an inventory reduction by TECNOL's largest company last year and how it would affect sales, a spokesman said.

In a statement, the company also said it expects to report sales of about $36 million and net income in a range of $3.0-$4.0 million, or $0.15-$0.20 per share for the third quarter. First Call listed analysts' consensus earnings forecast for the quarter at $0.25 a share.
TECNOL reported sales of $26.3 million and net income of $1.0 million, or $0.05 per share, in its fiscal 1995 third quarter. Its shares were off 3/8 at 15-7/8 in early trading.
The company said that it was unable to ship about $500,000 to $1.0 million of orders received in the third quarter as a result of production not reaching desired levels.

The company also said that, while gross margins are expected to improve in the third and fourth quarters of fiscal 1996 versus comparable 1995 periods, they are not expected to reach levels that were previously anticipated.
TECNOL said it believes the gross margin in the third quarter was affected by the mix of products shipped and the lower-than-expected production levels.

The impact of certain cost reduction programs being instituted this fiscal year have also been delayed, it said. Improvements in gross margin are now expected to occur in fiscal 1997, rather than in the second half of the current year, the company said.

It said the actual gross margin for the quarter ended August 31 has not been calculated and that its comments are based on preliminary estimates. It expects to report third quarter results the fourth week of September.
